Known gaps of the OPf_PARENS check: a paren on an op perl folds or
optimises away. A folded op carries no P bit, so psc's Paren on that node
has no counterpart; perigrin's ruling (2026-10-23, chain-review round 6,
F15) makes it a gap, never a defect, and canon writes the paren.

Each row is a fixture, as in fixtures.txt, with a `--- gap` section: the
`LINE OP` psc's Paren maps to, which perl folded away. The check re-runs
the pinned perl on the snippet and requires that op to be absent from the
statement's ops, or one of that name to carry FOLD; a row that perl still
emits present and unfolded fails. `#` lines quote perl 5.44.0's Concise,
the evidence of the fold.

=== a parenthesised hash key
my %h;
my $v = $h{(1)};
--- perl
none
--- gap
2 const
# 5           <+> multideref($h{"1"}) sK ->6: the key's const is folded
# into the multideref, and no op carries P

=== a negated parenthesised constant
my $v = -(1);
--- perl
none
--- gap
1 const
# 3        <$> const[IV -1] s/FOLD ->4

=== a concatenation with a parenthesised constant
my $v = "a" . ("b");
--- perl
none
--- gap
1 const
# 3        <$> const[PV "ab"] s/FOLD ->4

=== a parenthesised element before an arrow subscript
sub g {
  my $v = ($_[0])->[0];
}
--- perl
none
--- gap
2 aelem
# -           <1> ex-aelem sK/2 ->3
# 2              <+> multideref($_[0][0]) sK ->3: the aelem is nulled
# into the multideref, and no op carries P
